newsitem.title: REUNION: French water firm staff own up to party funding.
newsitem.headline: French water firm staff own up to party funding.

text.p: Two senior employees of French conglomerate Compagnie Generale des Eaux admitted in court on Wednesday that their group had funded elected officials on the French island of La Reunion.
The trial focuses on alleged corruption in a water deal on the island involving the water, building and telecommuniations giant and the Socialist town hall at Saint-Denis.

Jean-Dominique Deschamps, deputy director-general of the CGE, and director Jean-Pierre Tardieu had so far acknowledged paying some four million francs ($800,000) in 1991-93 to a company based in Djibouti.
They had testified that the money was payment for prospecting work on the CGE's behalf in the Horn of Africa.
"We knew that these sums were destined to a political party in Reunion," Deschamps admitted on Wednesday. He detailed payments made from 1991 onwards through Djibouti.
Tardieu said that in late 1990, around the time the CGE and a subsidiary signed big water contracts with the town hall, he had been told of a demand for "political funding".

Former mayor Gilbert Annette has acknowledged using the funds to pay back debts incurred during an election campaign and to meet urgent social needs in the town. Former CGE chairman Guy Dejouany was cleared of suspicion in July.
